sections.h2: What should a Utah home seller know about the state first?
sections.html:
Utah became the 45th state on January 4, 1896, and Salt Lake City is both the capital and the largest city. The 2020 census counted 3,271,616 residents across 84,899 square miles, according to Wikipedia's state article.

The state has 29 counties, and county government matters more to a seller than the state does. Counties assess property, bill and collect the tax, record deeds and run tax sales. A guide for Salt Lake County will not answer a Washington County question, so it helps to know which county the house sits in before reading anything else.

Most sellers deal with one of two regions: the Wasatch Front in the north and the Dixie area around St. George in the southwest.

Wikipedia describes the Wasatch Front as a strip about 110 miles long and 30 miles wide at its widest, running between the Wasatch Mountains and a western edge formed by Utah Lake, the Oquirrh Mountains and the Great Salt Lake. It lists Salt Lake, Utah, Davis, Weber and Box Elder counties in the region, with a 2020 population of 2,527,205. Interstate 15 and U.S. 89 run through the middle of it.

Dixie is the lowest and hottest part of the state. St. George sits there, and the state article puts its precipitation near 3 inches a year, against roughly 60 inches of snow in Salt Lake City.

  • Wasatch Front: Salt Lake City, Ogden, Provo, Orem, Layton, Bountiful.
  • Southwest or Dixie: St. George, plus nearby towns such as Hurricane and Washington.
  • Northern Utah beyond the Front: Logan, the base of the fifth largest metro area on Wikipedia's list.

sections.h2: How does Utah's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Utah is mostly dry, from semi-arid to desert, with very hot summers, cold winters and big swings between day and night temperatures.

On the Wasatch Front, Wikipedia notes lows of 0 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit in the urban corridor, mid-winter inversions that can trap cold air for weeks, and lake-effect snow from the Great Salt Lake in late fall and early winter. Summer highs run around 95 degrees with thunderstorms from early July through early September.

For a seller, that means two different inspection stories. A Salt Lake or Ogden house is judged on its heating, roof and winter wear, while a St. George house is judged on cooling and sun exposure. Buyers and appraisers in each region look at different things.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Utah?
sections.html:
County assessors value property, and the county auditor, treasurer and board of equalization handle notices, collection and appeals. The Utah State Tax Commission oversees the system and says it does not collect payments, so bills go to the county treasurer.

Homes that qualify as a primary residence get a 45% exemption, which leaves 55% of market value taxable. A household can claim only one such exemption in the state, and a vacation or second home does not qualify.

ItemRule
Valuation notice mailedOn or before July 22 each year
Appeal to county board of equalizationLater of September 15 or 45 days after the notice
Board decisionWithin 60 days of the application
Taxes dueNovember 30 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday)
Late penalty2.5% or $10, whichever is greater; 1% or $10 if paid by January 31
Interest after January 316% plus the federal funds rate, floor 7%, cap 10%

The statutes are Utah Code 59-2-919.1, 59-2-1004 and 59-2-1331. Owners who are 65 or older, disabled or in extreme hardship may be able to defer tax on a primary residence, and the valuation notice has to say so.

sections.h2: What does a Utah foreclosure look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Utah homes are usually foreclosed through a trust deed, which lets a trustee sell without a lawsuit. The trustee records a notice of default with the county recorder and must wait at least three months before giving notice of sale, under Utah Code 57-1-24.

The notice of sale has its own timing under 57-1-25. It must be posted at least 20 days before the sale, published weekly for three weeks, and the sale must take place at a courthouse serving the county between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

  • Month 0: notice of default recorded in the county where the house sits.
  • After three months: trustee may give notice of sale.
  • At least 20 days before the sale: notice posted on the property and at the recorder's office.
  • Sale day: held at a county courthouse, daytime hours only.

A seller who closes before that date avoids the auction. A cash buyer is one way to meet a short timeline.

sections.h2: What happens when Utah property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels can be sold by the county auditor. Under Utah Code 59-2-1351.1 an accepted bid must cover the taxes, notice charges, penalties, interest and administrative costs, and surplus proceeds are treated as unclaimed property.

Before it gets there, a county legislative body can reduce or defer delinquent taxes when the public interest is served. A deferral needs written consent from any mortgage or trust deed holder, becomes a lien and is due when the property is sold, according to Utah Code 59-2-1347.

sections.h2: How do Utah's other guides fit together?
sections.html:
The statewide pages cover rules that apply across counties: property tax appeals, the homestead exemption, estate and inheritance tax, eviction, capital gains, tax sales and probate. The city and county pages narrow that down to where the house actually is.

The homestead rules, for example, come from state law. Utah Code 78B-5-503 protects up to $42,000 of a primary residence from creditors, and $84,000 for a jointly owned home per household, before inflation adjustments. County offices then apply the property tax rules locally.

  • Use a county page when the question is about assessment, tax bills, appeals or the recorder.
  • Use a city page when the question is about the local market, neighborhoods or how a sale there usually goes.
  • Use a state page when the question is about a statute, such as eviction notice periods or a trust deed sale.

Cities on this site include the large Wasatch Front names such as Salt Lake City, Provo and Ogden, and southern ones such as St. George, Cedar City and Hurricane.

faqs.q: How many counties does Utah have?
faqs.a: Utah has 29 counties. Salt Lake County is the most populous at 1,220,916 people in the 2020 census, and San Juan County is the largest by area at 7,820 square miles.

faqs.q: When are Utah property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 each year, or the next day that is not a weekend or holiday. Tax paid late carries a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, and that drops to 1% or $10 if paid by January 31.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Utah property valuation?
faqs.a: File with the county board of equalization by the later of September 15 or 45 days after the county auditor's valuation notice. Include your estimate of fair market value and any evidence of unequal treatment. The board has 60 days to decide, and you can then appeal to the Tax Commission.

faqs.q: How long does a Utah trust deed foreclosure take?
faqs.a: At least three months from the recorded notice of default before notice of sale can be given, then at least 20 days of posting before the sale. The exact calendar depends on the lender and the county.

faqs.q: Does Utah's primary residence exemption transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commission says the exemption does not carry over to new owners, who must file their own application. Starting January 1, 2027, an ownership change also triggers a filing on form TC-473A with the county board of equalization.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Utah house for cash if it is behind on taxes or in default?
faqs.a: Yes, an owner can sell as-is while taxes are delinquent or a notice of default is on record, as long as the sale closes before the county or trustee sale. Cash Home Buyers can review the situation and explain what a closing would involve.
